analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: fresh outlooks
key_insights: US stocks traded higher Thursday 11/12 as investors looked through the NVDA management transition and the AI complex, and through a 10bp jump in the US 10-year Treasury yield to 5.10%. Bond markets are still reacting to Tuesday's strong CPI report.
GS economists added a third Fed funds rate hike in a late Tuesday note, 'Adding a Third Hike in March'.

Today's data was benign and not what is moving rates. Existing home sales fell 5.5% in October, somewhat below expectations and the lowest level since July 2010. GS expects higher mortgage rates to substantially depress housing turnover.
On the existing home sales release, GS economists cut their Q4 GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +1.8% q/q annualized.

NVDA opened down 13% and recovered to about -5%. Jim Schneider calls the management transition announcement a meaningful but measured negative. He sees higher execution risk over the next 12-18 months and more difficulty negotiating new multi-party ecosystem investments at the same scale as before.
GS maintains its Buy on NVDA after a 20% drop this month and a 12% decline ytd.

Historical analog for NVDA: Apple de-rated from about 17x to about 12x NTM P/E over the ~18 months before Steve Jobs' death in October 2011 (he went on medical leave in January 2011). It traded as low as about 9x NTM P/E in 2013, then recovered to about 15x once execution continuity was clear.

Global Macro Outlook 2027 (Hatzius, Wilson): global growth of 2.8% in 2027 after 2.7% in 2026. Lower energy prices and strong AI capex drive the baseline. Downside risks are renewed energy shocks, fiscal stress, AI investment disappointment and early labor-market pressure. Central banks are expected to pivot back to cuts late in 2027. 2027 growth may be the cycle peak, and GS advises hedging against downside events.

Global Equity Strategy 2027 Outlook (Oppenheimer): S&P 500 EPS growth slows to 11% in 2027 from 36% this year. GS says markets have already priced much of the slowdown, and moderating inflation with lower bond yields should support upside. It favors long-duration Growth, especially US hyperscalers, balanced with selective Defensives. It is overweight the US and Japan and underweight Europe.

Commodity Views 2027 Outlook (Struyven): the base case of further energy price moderation implies near-zero total commodity returns in 2027, after +26% ytd in 2026. Base case 2027 average Brent is $88/bbl and European TTF gas is 45EUR/MWh. GS sees upside to copper ($15,600/t by Dec27) and gold ($4,650/toz by Dec27). It argues commodities still hedge geopolitical escalation, winter supply shocks and US-China power race constraints.

China 2027 Outlook (Hui Shan): real GDP growth of 4.5%, helped by a smaller property drag (-1.3pp vs -1.8pp in 2026) and less fiscal tightening. Resilient exports and subdued CPI inflation of 0.5% favor lower domestic rates and gradual CNY appreciation.

Chart of the day (Rindels): GS forecasts above-consensus business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4 in 2027, but only a 0.2pp boost to measured GDP growth from AI capex. Counting semiconductor investment, chip design service exports and spillovers, it estimates AI spending adds 0.6pp to real GDP growth in both 2026 and 2027.
Midday performance on 11/12: S&P 500 +0.2% (1 month -2.2%, YTD +11.6%), DJIA +0.4%, Nasdaq +0.1% (1 month -6.4%), Russell 2000 -0.8%.
Calendar: Friday brings October PPI. AMAT, CSCO, FLNT, GEMI, HAWK, KLC, LVLU, OFRM, RLMD and YSS report after the close Thursday, and ACCV before the open Friday.

tension_points.bull_case: Global growth of 2.8% in 2027, lower energy prices and strong AI capex keep the baseline steady. Moderating inflation and lower yields support equity upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Downside risks include renewed energy shocks, fiscal stress, AI investment disappointment and early labor-market pressure. GS notes that 2027 growth may be the peak of this cycle.

tension_points.bull_case: NVDA has strong functional leadership and a well-defined product roadmap. The Apple analog shows multiples recovered once execution continuity was clear. GS keeps its Buy.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher execution risk over the next 12-18 months. It may be harder to negotiate new multi-party ecosystem investments at the same scale. The Apple analog de-rated from about 17x to about 12x NTM P/E, and as low as about 9x.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of execution continuity on products would support the recovery case, per the Apple analog.

Global growth stays resilient but uneven in 2027 on lower energy prices and strong AI capex, with downside risks.
